passage: The prize distribution at the school hall in Indore ran late because the sound system kept crackling. Rukmini, five, walked back from the stage with her medal, chest out, chin up, marching like a soldier. Her father Kamal, holding a cold drink, clapped. On the way out, a group of older children crowded near. Rukmini's chest sank, and she stepped behind Kamal's leg, holding the medal against her tummy. He said quietly, "You can show them when you're ready." After a minute, she peeked out and held the medal up.

qa.q: What did Rukmini do with her chest when she walked back from the stage?
qa.a: She walked back with her chest out and her chin up.

qa.q: What does Rukmini's stepping behind her father's leg suggest she felt when the older children crowded round?
qa.a: It suggests she felt shy or wary, since her chest sank and she held the medal to her tummy. She might also simply have been tired after the long event.

qa.q: What could Kamal do to help Rukmini in a crowd?
qa.a: He can let her take her time behind him and invite her to show the medal when she is ready, as he did.

qa.q: How might the older children see Rukmini's marching walk?
qa.a: They may see a proud small girl, and might not realise she felt shy when they crowded round.

grounding: A preschooler shows pride through posture and shrinks when shy, and a gentle warm-up time helps.

passage: After scoring at the colony's cricket match, Sunaina, six, stood tall by the wicket, hands on hips, shoulders back, grinning at her father Vikas at the boundary. "Did you see?" she called. "I saw!" he said. Then a tall neighbour boy asked her to bat again in front of the whole crowd. Her shoulders rounded and her hands went to her sides. She looked at Vikas. "Maybe later," he told the boy. Sunaina smiled and sat down beside him, relaxed.

qa.q: Where was Vikas when Sunaina scored?
qa.a: He was at the boundary.

qa.q: What does Sunaina's change of posture suggest about her feelings?
qa.a: Standing tall with hands on hips suggests pride in her score. Rounded shoulders and looking at her father suggest she felt shy or under pressure when asked to bat in front of the crowd.

qa.q: What could Vikas do to support Sunaina's shyness?
qa.a: He can do as he did, protecting her from the pressure and letting her decide when she is ready to perform again.

qa.q: How might the neighbour boy feel when Sunaina doesn't bat again?
qa.a: He may feel a little let down, but he may also have just wanted more of the fun.

grounding: Posture shows pride after a success and shyness under pressure, and a shy child needs warm-up time.

passage:
“Uday Chacha, look!”
Rafiq stood in the hall with every button of his shirt done up, chest pushed out, chin high.
“You did all of them yourself?”
“All by myself!” He puffed his chest even more and marched in a circle.
“Wah! Come show Dadi's friends.”
In the next room were four ladies with tea. Rafiq stopped at the door, and his chest sank. He slid behind Uday's leg and peeked out.
“Okay,” said Uday quietly. “Show them later, when you're ready.”
Rafiq nodded into his knee.

qa.q: What had Rafiq done all by himself?
qa.a: He had done up every button of his shirt.

qa.q: What changed in Rafiq's feelings when he reached the door?
qa.a: He went from proud and bold, chest out, to shy and wary in front of four strangers, which is why he hid behind Uday's leg.

qa.q: Which choice by Uday worked, and why?
qa.a: He let Rafiq show the buttons later instead of pushing him to perform, giving him time to warm up.

qa.q: What would change if Uday had pulled Rafiq into the room?
qa.a: Rafiq might feel embarrassed and upset, and his proud moment could turn into a bad one.

grounding: A preschooler stands tall with chest out after a success, then hides behind an adult's leg when shy, and is given warm-up time.

passage:
Note by Jyoti, nursery teacher, after family day.
This week Farhan finally climbed to the top of the climbing frame. He stood up there with his chest out and fists on his hips, shouting, “I'm the king!” Today, at family day, I asked him to show the parents. He walked to the frame, saw the crowd, and pressed himself behind my legs. I told him, “You can just watch today.” After the parents had moved on to the art table, he climbed it quietly and waved to his mother from the top.

qa.q: What did Farhan shout from the top of the climbing frame?
qa.a: “I'm the king!”

qa.q: What was Farhan feeling when he pressed himself behind Jyoti's legs?
qa.a: He felt shy and wary with the crowd of parents watching, even though he had felt proud and bold when he climbed alone.

qa.q: What went right in how Jyoti handled the moment?
qa.a: Jyoti didn't push him to perform and let him watch, and he chose to climb once the crowd moved away.

qa.q: How might Farhan's mother feel when he waved from the top?
qa.a: She was probably proud and happy to see him do it in his own time.

grounding: The teacher's note shows a child's proud chest-out stance after a success and his shrinking with a crowd, eased by warm-up time.

passage: Raghav carried the small brass pot of water all the way from the hand pump without spilling. At the door he set it down and stood tall, chest puffed, grinning at Jyoti Dadi. “Shabash!” she said. That evening at the temple, the priest asked the children to sing. Raghav's chest caved in. He grabbed the end of Dadi's sari and hid behind her. Dadi stroked his head. “He'll sing another day,” she told the priest. On the walk home, Raghav sang loudly to the buffaloes.

qa.q: What did Raghav carry from the hand pump?
qa.a: The small brass pot of water.

qa.q: How can you tell that Raghav felt proud when he set down the pot?
qa.a: He stood tall with his chest puffed and grinned at Dadi. Later, at the temple, his caved-in chest showed he felt shy instead.

qa.q: What did Dadi do that helped Raghav?
qa.a: She stroked his head and told the priest he would sing another day, protecting him from pressure.

qa.q: How might the priest see Raghav hiding?
qa.a: The priest might see it as ordinary shyness in a small child and not mind, especially after Dadi's words.

grounding: A child stands tall after a success but shrinks behind his grandmother when asked to perform, and she gives him time.

passage:
At the swimming pool in Porto, Sofia kicked her way across the whole width for the first time. She climbed out, stood tall with her chest pushed out and her hands on her hips, dripping and grinning at her mother.

"You did it!" Beatriz said.

That afternoon, at a cousin's birthday, the same girl hid behind her mother's leg, peeking out at the crowd of children.

"Go and say hello," an aunt urged.

"She'll go when she's ready," Beatriz said, and stroked her hair. Twenty minutes later Sofia was chasing balloons.

qa.q: Where did Sofia swim across the whole width for the first time?
qa.a: At the swimming pool in Porto.

qa.q: What was Sofia feeling when she stood with her chest out and hands on her hips?
qa.a: She was most likely proud of her first full width. Later, hiding behind her mother's leg shows she felt shy and wary in a crowd of children.

qa.q: Which choice worked at the birthday, and why?
qa.a: Beatriz let Sofia warm up in her own time instead of pushing her, and she joined the balloon chase once she felt ready.

qa.q: How does the aunt see Sofia's hiding compared with Beatriz?
qa.a: The aunt thinks Sofia just needs a push to say hello, while Beatriz sees a shy child who needs time.

grounding: It shows a preschooler standing tall with pride after a success and hiding behind a leg when shy, with warm-up time instead of pressure.
